purpose: H1 (seed initialization) + H2 (respiration native rate) remediation outcome, Day 12.

h1.root_cause: Every Sleep-EDF trainer constructs SleepStageClassifier(...) BEFORE calling torch.manual_seed(seed) (which happens inside train_one(), only after construction). Model weight initialization consumes torch's global RNG at construction time, so the recorded seed does not control initial weights - only DataLoader shuffle order (correct) and the already-independently-seeded EOG shuffle (correct, uses its own np.random.default_rng) are actually seed-controlled.
h1.affected_claims: Exact seed-controlled-retraining reproducibility claims (i.e. 'rerunning seed42 from a fresh process reproduces the exact same initial weights') were unsupported. Existing checkpoint-based EVALUATION reproducibility (reload a saved checkpoint, re-evaluate, compare metrics) was NEVER affected - that only depends on the saved weights being read correctly, not on how they were originally initialized.

reproduction_probe.method: Real test: constructs the actual SleepStageClassifier and reads its actual initial Conv1d weights under the buggy order (bug reproduced) and the corrected order (fix confirmed), across different simulated ambient RNG states.

corrected_protocol.rationale_for_not_modifying_historical_t: Editing them in place would itself be a form of rewriting the historical record of what actually produced the existing checkpoints. The corrected protocol lives only in the new module/script; any future Sleep-EDF training should use it.

retraining_performed.scope: Bounded diagnostic: Primary A (EEG-only) and B (EEG+EOG), 5 seeds each (42-46), same split/architecture/preprocessing/epochs/optimizer/hyperparameters as the original - only seeding order changed.
retraining_performed.checkpoints: ml/checkpoints/sleep_edf_{baseline_eeg_only,candidate_eeg_plus_eog}_seedfix_v2_seed{42-46}.pt (10 new files, NEVER overwrite the original 10)
not_retrained_this_sprint: Shuffled-EOG control C (5 checkpoints) - PENDING_FOLLOWUP, not diagnosed this sprint due to time constraints. The EOG shuffle mechanism itself (np.random.default_rng) was NEVER affected by H1 - only C's model initialization is unverified under the corrected protocol.

Interaction M_B/M_AB (10 checkpoints) - PENDING_FOLLOWUP, same reasoning; the interaction result's capacity-fairness and Resp-bandwidth findings are unaffected by H1 (those depend on parameter counts and data content, not initialization), but exact seed-controlled reproducibility for M_B/M_AB specifically remains unverified.

primary_subject_level.note: SC4011 remains the dominant, most consistently favorable subject under both the original and corrected protocol; SC4081/SC4131 remain small/mixed under both.

primary_class_level.REM_pattern: Largest class-level gain under both protocols (4/5 seeds improve under corrected protocol, matching the original's REM-dominant pattern).
primary_class_level.N3_pattern: Flat-to-slightly-improving in the PRIMARY cohort under both protocols (N3 regression was only ever observed in the SECONDARY holdout cohort, not primary - unaffected by this diagnostic's scope).

corrected_vs_original_comparison.conclusion: The corrected-seed protocol preserves the qualitative scientific conclusion (positive EOG effect, 4/5-seed-consistent, SC4011-dominated, REM-driven) exactly. Numerical values differ modestly (as expected - these are now genuinely different, correctly-seeded trained models, not a re-derivation of the same numbers) but do not change direction, seed-favor count, subject dominance pattern, or class pattern.

h1.canonical_migration: Historical results/sleep_edf_eeg_eog_ablation.json REMAINS the canonical, cited artifact - not deprecated, not deleted. results/sleep_edf_primary_seedfix_v2.json is ADDED as confirmatory, fully-seed-controlled evidence. Future citations MAY prefer the seedfix_v2 numbers as the more rigorously provenanced version; this is a recommendation, not a mandate, since both currently show the same qualitative finding.

h2.root_cause: Resp oro-nasal is natively 1 Hz (confirmed via EDF header: 30 samples/30s record), not 100 Hz as originally stated. EEG/EOG are genuinely natively 100 Hz (3000 samples/30s record). MNE's raw.info['sfreq'] reports one global common-grid rate (100 Hz) for the whole file regardless of per-channel native rate - conflating LOADED_COMMON_GRID_RATE with NATIVE_SIGNAL_RATE caused the original error.
h2.mne_behavior: mne.io.edf.edf._read_segment_file upsamples any channel whose native sample count is below the file's maximum, via mne.filter.resample (FFT-based, npad=0), after all chunks are loaded (avoiding preload=False edge artifacts - this project's loader always uses preload=True).

data_impact.why: The interaction training script has always called load_dataset_windows_multi(..., preload=True), which has always produced exactly this FFT-upsampled 100 Hz Resp representation. The fix is metadata/documentation only - new constants (RESP_NATIVE_SFREQ_HZ=1.0, RESP_LOADED_SFREQ_HZ=100.0, RESP_RESAMPLING_METHOD, EEG_EOG_NATIVE_SFREQ_HZ=100.0) added to ml/datasets/sleep_edf.py are purely additive; no function body was touched (verified by direct code review of the diff and by re-running the loader post-edit, producing a correctly-shaped array with no errors).

fixed_documents: docs/INTERACTION_EXPERIMENT_FEASIBILITY_DAY10.md (struck-through correction, original text preserved visibly, not silently edited)
h2.interpretation_impact: approximately_additive_or_unresolved is UNCHANGED - not strengthened by this correction. New disclosed limitation: Resp's 1 Hz native bandwidth is a plausible contributing explanation for Candidate B (Resp alone) showing no clear benefit, offered as a plausible explanation, not a proven mechanism.

freeze_impact: See results/scientific_freeze_candidate_post_audit_day12.json for the formal freeze-status determination.
required_canonical_migration: None mandatory. Optional: prefer results/sleep_edf_primary_seedfix_v2.json for future citations of the primary EEG-vs-EEG+EOG comparison, since it carries fully-verified seed provenance; the original results/sleep_edf_eeg_eog_ablation.json remains valid and is not deprecated.
